title: Inwangsan city-wall sunset
name: Inwangsan
cool: A short climb along the Joseon-era city wall to granite boulders where Gyeongbokgung, Namsan Tower and the whole city fit in one frame. Golden hour up here is unforgettable.
catch: ≈1.5–2 h up and down, almost all stairs. The way down after sunset is dark (phone torch) and the top is windy and cold in November.
swap: Thu 29 Oct after the palaces, instead of Insadong — start right behind Gyeongbokgung.
metro: Line 3 → Gyeongbokgung or Dongnimmun, then 10 min to the trail.

title: Seochon & Tongin Market lunchbox
name: Tongin Traditional Market
cool: Buy a tray and a string of old brass coins (≈₩10,000 for 20), fill it with bites from the market stalls, then wander Seochon's quiet hanok lanes and old bookshops.
catch: The lunchbox café runs late morning to mid-afternoon and some stalls close early. It's 5 min from Tosokchon, so pick one lunch.
swap: Thu 29 Oct lunch instead of Tosokchon or Sujebi.

title: National Museum of Korea
name: National Museum of Korea
cool: Huge, free and beautifully designed: Silla gold crowns, a ten-storey marble pagoda indoors, the hushed 'Room of Quiet Contemplation' with two Buddhas, and N Seoul Tower framed over the mirror pond.
catch: Easy to lose 3 hours here, and Ichon is a little off your routes. Late opening (till 21:00) only on Wednesdays and Saturdays.
swap: The perfect rainy-day backup for any Seoul day — Line 4 from Myeongdong runs straight there.
metro: Line 4 Myeongdong → Ichon (≈15 min, no change).

title: Garosu-gil ginkgo avenue
name: Garosu-gil
cool: Gangnam's tree-lined boutique street. The ginkgo trees turn gold right around your dates — small Korean labels, concept stores and good coffee under a yellow canopy.
catch: It's mostly shopping and cafés. Fallen ginkgo fruit smells on the pavement in autumn.
swap: Sun 1 Nov morning instead of Common Ground (≈15–20 min by taxi from the Seongsu hotel).

title: Starfield Library
name: Starfield Library
cool: Thirteen-metre bookshelves rising through the middle of COEX mall — one of Seoul's most photographed interiors. Free and open until 22:00.
catch: More attraction than quiet library, and busy at weekends. Around it is a very big mall.
swap: Sun 1 Nov — Line 2 runs straight from Konkuk Univ. Pair it with Bongeunsa across the road.
metro: Line 2 Konkuk Univ. → Samseong (≈15 min, no change).

title: Bongeunsa Temple
name: Bongeunsa Temple
cool: A 1,200-year-old temple facing Gangnam's glass towers: lantern-filled courtyards, a giant standing Buddha and quiet paths. Lovely in the evening when the lanterns glow.
catch: It overlaps with Jogyesa, which is already an option on Thu 29 — choose one temple in Seoul.
swap: With Starfield Library on Sun 1 Nov (5 min walk apart).
metro: Line 9 → Bongeunsa, or 10 min walk from Samseong (Line 2).

title: Leeum Museum of Art
name: Leeum Museum of Art
cool: Korean celadon and Joseon porcelain in Mario Botta's rotunda, modern art in buildings by Jean Nouvel and Rem Koolhaas, and a stunning museum shop.
catch: Closed Mondays; tickets are timed, so book online. It sits next to Itaewon — avoid the evening of Sat 31 Oct.
swap: Fri 30 Oct morning, or Thu 5 Nov afternoon after check-in.

title: Itaewon & Hannam-dong
name: Itaewon-dong
cool: Seoul's most international neighbourhood: Hannam-dong's design shops and cafés, rooftop bars with Namsan views and food from everywhere.
catch: Do not go on Sat 31 Oct — Halloween night here is extremely crowded. On other days it's fine, but it feels less Korean than the rest of the trip.
swap: Thu 5 Nov evening, together with Leeum.

title: Yeonnam-dong & Gyeongui Line Forest Park
name: Gyeongui Line Forest Park
cool: An old railway line turned into a long ribbon of park: picnic lawns, buskers, tiny bars and cafés, with Hongdae's indie street scene right next door.
catch: Hongdae gets very crowded at night and is one of the busiest Halloween spots on Sat 31 Oct. Go on a weekday afternoon.
swap: Fri 30 Oct instead of Myeongdong shopping.
metro: Line 2 Euljiro 1-ga → Hongik Univ. (≈20 min, no change), exit 3.

title: Ewha campus 'valley' & Sinchon
name: Ewha Womans University ECC
cool: Dominique Perrault's campus complex: a building sunk into the ground on both sides of a giant stairway. Dramatic photos, then student cafés in Sinchon.
catch: It's a working university — be quiet and stay out of buildings. A 30-minute stop, not a half day.
swap: On the way to Yeonnam-dong (Line 2, 2 stops).
metro: Line 2 → Ewha Womans Univ., 5 min walk.

title: Mangwon Market & a river sunset
name: Mangwon Market
cool: A truly local food market — croquettes, tteokbokki, crispy chicken gangjeong — then a 15-minute walk to Mangwon Hangang Park for a sunset picnic. Cheap, low-key, very Seoul.
catch: West side (≈20 min by taxi, ≈35 min by metro from Myeongdong), and it overlaps with the Yeouido river sunset already planned for Fri 30.
swap: Fri 30 Oct evening instead of Yeouido.

title: Haneul Park silver grass
name: Haneul Park
cool: A former landfill turned 'sky park'. In late October and early November the hilltop is a sea of silver grass that glows at sunset, with the Han River below.
catch: Far west (≈30 min by taxi, ≈45 min by metro from Myeongdong), with 291 zig-zag steps or a small paid shuttle up. Little else nearby — it's a half day for one sunset.
swap: Fri 30 Oct afternoon instead of Yeouido and the cruise — both are sunset slots, so pick one.
metro: Line 6 → World Cup Stadium (exit 1), 20 min walk + stairs.

title: Noryangjin Fish Market
name: Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market
cool: Seoul's giant wholesale seafood hall: aisles of tanks with crabs, abalone and fish; pick downstairs, eat it cooked upstairs. Spectacular to walk through.
catch: You already have two fish markets in Busan. Prices are per kilo and easily blow the ₩38k food budget — agree the price before they cut.
swap: Only if you drop one of the Busan fish markets.
price: Seafood per kg — easily over budget
metro: Line 1 or 9 → Noryangjin, footbridge to the market.

title: Achasan sunrise ridge
name: Achasan
cool: A gentle ridge near your Seongsu–Konkuk hotel (trailhead ≈15 min by taxi), with views over the Han River bridges and red maples. About 45–50 minutes to the top.
catch: Best at sunrise (≈06:50 in early November), which means an early alarm after the drone show. Some rocky steps.
swap: Sun 1 Nov morning instead of the sleep-in.
metro: Line 5 → Achasan or Gwangnaru, 15 min to the trailhead.

title: Lotte World Adventure
name: Lotte World
cool: An indoor theme park plus a castle on a lake island, right next to Seoul Sky. Korean couples rent matching school uniforms for it — silly, nostalgic and fun.
catch: A day pass costs ≈₩67,000 per person, queues are long, and Sunday is the busiest day. Wrong vibe if you want calm.
swap: Sun 1 Nov instead of Seokchon Lake and Seoul Sky (same block in Jamsil).

title: Hwadam Forest in autumn
name: Hwadamsup
cool: One of Korea's most loved autumn gardens: gentle paths through maples, pond bridges and a small monorail. Peak colour lands right around early November.
catch: ≈1 h by car outside Seoul. Timed tickets sell out in foliage season and foreigners report trouble booking online — a tour shuttle is the easy way. Closed Mondays.
swap: Sun 1 Nov instead of Jamsil (closest from the Konkuk hotel).
go: ≈1 h by car from the Seongsu–Konkuk hotel; easiest with a shuttle tour from Seoul.

title: Bukhansan · Baegundae peak
name: Baegundae Peak
cool: An 836 m granite summit inside the city limits. In late October the ridges are red and gold and you look down on all of Seoul.
catch: 4–5 h round trip with steep rock sections on cables; real hiking shoes needed. Trailhead ≈1 h from the centre and busy at weekends. Tough for a relaxed trip.
swap: Only as a whole-day swap, e.g. Fri 30 Oct instead of the slow river day.
go: ≈1 h from the centre: Line 4 → Seongsin Women's Univ., then Ui LRT → Bukhansan Ui and 15 min to the Baegun trail.

title: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress
name: Paldalmun Gate
cool: A UNESCO-listed 18th-century fortress: walk 5.7 km of ramparts, gates and watchtowers above the city, try traditional archery, and end on Suwon's famous fried-chicken alley.
catch: ≈1–1.5 h each way, and the full wall walk is 2–3 h with hills. It's a whole-day swap.
swap: Fri 30 Oct instead of the Myeongdong/Yeouido day.
go: ≈1 h: Line 1 or an ITX/KTX train from Seoul Station to Suwon (≈30–60 min), then bus/taxi 10 min.

title: Nami Island
name: Nami Island
cool: A small river island famous for its tree-lined avenues of ginkgo and redwood in autumn — you can even arrive by zipline.
catch: ≈1.5–2 h each way (ITX train to Gapyeong + taxi + ferry) and peak-foliage crowds. It eats a whole Seoul day.
swap: Whole day instead of Fri 30 Oct.
go: ≈1.5–2 h: ITX-Cheongchun from Yongsan or Cheongnyangni to Gapyeong, taxi 5 min, ferry 5 min.

title: DMZ tour
name: Imjingak Tourist Information Center
cool: Stand at the edge of the world's last Cold War frontier: Imjingak, the Freedom Bridge, tunnels and observatories. A powerful history lesson.
catch: Guided tours only (passport, book days ahead), a full day of 8–10 h, and programmes change at short notice. Emotionally heavy — the opposite of a relaxed couple trip.
swap: Probably not this time.
go: Tour bus from central Seoul, ≈1–1.5 h each way.

title: Gyeongju day trip
name: Bulguksa
cool: The ancient Silla capital: Bulguksa temple in autumn colour, the grassy royal tomb mounds of Daereungwon, Hwangnidan-gil cafés, and Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond glowing at night.
catch: Singyeongju station is outside town (buses 35–40 min to the sights). It's a full day that replaces Wed 4 Nov (Gamcheon & Jagalchi).
swap: Wed 4 Nov, instead of colourful old Busan.
go: ≈30 min by KTX from Busan Station to Singyeongju, then bus or taxi 35–40 min.

title: Beomeosa mountain temple
name: Beomeosa Temple
cool: A 1,300-year-old temple on Geumjeongsan: maple-lined stairs, quiet courtyards and almost no crowds — the calm opposite of Haedong Yonggungsa.
catch: ≈40 min by taxi or ≈1 h by metro from Gwangalli. If you only want one temple in Busan, it competes with Haedong Yonggungsa.
swap: Tue 3 Nov instead of Haedong Yonggungsa.
metro: Line 2 → Seomyeon, Line 1 → Beomeosa, then a short bus or taxi up the hill.

title: Oryukdo Skywalk
name: Oryukdo Skywalk
cool: A glass horseshoe hanging over the cliffs where the East Sea meets the South Sea, facing the five little Oryuk islets. Free, and the start of the Igidae coastal trail.
catch: Short stop (20–30 min); closes at 18:00 and in strong wind. Shoe covers on the glass, no selfie sticks.
swap: Mon 2 Nov with the Igidae walk — it's the far end of the same trail.
metro: Taxi ≈20 min from the hotel, or a city bus from Gwangalli.

title: Ahopsan bamboo forest
name: Ahopsan Forest
cool: A private family forest of tall bamboo and old pines with a stone gate you may recognise from K-dramas. Green, hushed, beautiful light.
catch: Far north-east in Gijang (≈35 min by taxi from Gwangalli, over an hour by bus). Entry ≈₩8,000; it's a walk and photos, nothing more.
swap: Tue 3 Nov after Haedong Yonggungsa (both in Gijang).

title: Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower
name: Busan Tower
cool: A hilltop park above Nampo reached by outdoor escalators; the tower gives a 360° harbour view. Five minutes from Jagalchi and BIFF Square.
catch: Tower ticket extra, and the view is less dramatic than BUSAN X the SKY — choose one observatory.
swap: Wed 4 Nov right after the Jagalchi lunch.
metro: Walk 5 min from Nampo (Line 1) via the Gwangbok-ro escalators.
